subject: Business Communication
notes: Communication skills core. No numerical questions apply; extra objective and case items included.

questions.text: The process of exchanging ideas facts and feelings between two or more people is called
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Communication is the transfer and understanding of meaning between people.

questions.text: In the communication process the person who initiates the message is the
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: The sender encodes and transmits the message to the receiver.

questions.text: The response of the receiver that confirms whether the message was understood is called
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Feedback completes the communication loop and lets the sender verify understanding.

questions.text: Communication is a two way process
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Effective communication involves both sending and receiving with feedback.

questions.text: State the elements of the communication process
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Sender message encoding channel decoding receiver and feedback.
questions.explanation: These seven elements make up the complete communication cycle.

questions.text: Explain the importance of communication in business
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Communication helps in planning decision making coordination and motivation. It builds relationships with customers and suppliers and is essential for leadership and change management.
questions.explanation: Cover internal coordination and external stakeholder relations.

questions.text: Noise in communication refers to
questions.subject: Business Communication
options: Any interference that distorts the message
questions.explanation: Noise is any barrier that distorts or interrupts the message.

questions.text: Using jargon that the receiver does not understand is which type of barrier
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Semantic barriers arise from words and symbols having different meanings.

questions.text: The C of communication that means the message should contain all the facts the receiver needs is
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Completeness ensures the receiver has everything required to act or decide.

questions.text: Selective perception is a psychological barrier to communication
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: People filter information through their own attitudes and expectations causing selective perception.

questions.text: List the seven Cs of effective communication
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Completeness conciseness consideration concreteness clarity courtesy and correctness.
questions.explanation: These seven Cs guide effective message construction.

questions.text: Explain the barriers to effective communication and how to overcome them
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Barriers may be semantic physical psychological or organisational. They are overcome by using simple language active listening empathy the right channel and encouraging feedback.
questions.explanation: Cover each barrier type and the matching remedy.

questions.text: A formal written message sent inside an organisation is called a
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: A memorandum or memo is used for internal written communication.

questions.text: The part of a business letter that contains the main message is the
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: The body carries the main content between the salutation and the close.

questions.text: A report that is prepared in a prescribed form at regular intervals is a
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Routine reports are submitted periodically in a standard format.

questions.text: A memo is usually addressed to people outside the organisation
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Memos are internal documents; external messages use letters.

questions.text: What are the parts of a formal business letter
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Heading date inside address salutation subject body complimentary close and signature.
questions.explanation: These standard parts give a letter its formal structure.

questions.text: Explain the different types of business reports
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Reports may be routine or special formal or informal and informational or analytical. They differ in frequency format and whether they merely present facts or also interpret them.
questions.explanation: Classify reports by frequency form and purpose.

questions.text: The style of communication in which a speaker addresses a live audience is called
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: A presentation is a structured oral communication to an audience.

questions.text: Non verbal communication that studies body movement is called
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Kinesics is the study of gestures posture and body language.

questions.text: Eye contact is an important element of effective public speaking
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Eye contact engages the audience and builds credibility and rapport.

questions.text: List the characteristics of effective presentation
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Clear objective logical structure confident delivery audience awareness and effective use of visual aids.
questions.explanation: These characteristics keep the audience engaged and informed.

questions.text: Explain the importance of non verbal communication
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Non verbal cues such as facial expression gestures posture and tone often convey more than words and can reinforce or contradict the spoken message. They build trust and express emotions.
questions.explanation: Cover the types of non verbal cues and their impact on meaning.

questions.text: Electronic mail is an example of
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Email is a form of electronic written communication.

questions.text: The informal communication network that spreads by word of mouth is called the
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: The grapevine is the unofficial channel of communication within an organisation.

questions.text: An email should have a clear and relevant subject line
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: A clear subject line helps the receiver prioritise and understand the message.

questions.text: Differentiate between formal and informal communication
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Formal communication follows the official chain of command and is documented. Informal communication is unofficial and spontaneous and moves through the grapevine.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in official structure and documentation.

questions.text: Explain the advantages and limitations of email communication
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Email is fast inexpensive and provides a written record with easy sharing. Its limits include misinterpretation lack of non verbal cues and information overload.
questions.explanation: Balance the speed and record benefits against the loss of personal touch.

questions.text: A group discussion is an effective tool used mainly for
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Group discussions evaluate communication leadership and team skills.

questions.text: The first formal stage of a selection interview is usually the
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: A screening interview is the preliminary stage to shortlist candidates.

questions.text: In a group discussion dominating others and not allowing them to speak is a positive trait
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Dominating a discussion is negative; balanced participation and listening are valued.

questions.text: List any four do s for a successful job interview
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Arrive on time dress appropriately maintain eye contact and answer clearly with relevant examples.
questions.explanation: These behaviours create a positive impression on the interviewer.

questions.text: Explain the skills required to succeed in a group discussion
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Success requires listening analytical thinking clarity of expression leadership and the ability to cooperate. A candidate must present views logically and respect others while steering the discussion.
questions.explanation: Cover the communication and behavioural skills assessed in a GD.

questions.text: Assertion: Listening is as important as speaking in communication. Reason: Communication is complete only when the receiver accurately understands the message
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.topic: Nature and importance of communication (assertion reason)
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: Understanding depends on listening so listening is central to complete communication.

questions.text: Match the communication element to its role
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Encoding converts the idea into a message while decoding interprets it.

questions.text: A meeting notice that is displayed on a board for all employees is called a
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: A notice is a public written announcement displayed for information.

questions.text: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting is called the
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: An agenda lists the topics in the order they will be taken up at the meeting.

questions.text: Minutes of a meeting are a written record of what was discussed and decided
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Minutes are the official record of proceedings and resolutions of a meeting.

questions.text: State the difference between a notice and a circular
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: A notice is displayed publicly for a wide audience while a circular is distributed to a specific group or department.
questions.explanation: The difference is in the audience and the method of distribution.

questions.text: Read the case: A manager sends a long email full of technical jargon to a new intern who misreads an important deadline. Identify the barriers and suggest how the message could be improved
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: The barriers are semantic from jargon and possible overload from length. The manager should use simple language a clear subject line and highlight the deadline explicitly then request confirmation.
questions.explanation: Apply the seven Cs to rewrite the message for clarity.

questions.text: Read the case: During a presentation the audience looks confused when the speaker uses a technical chart with no labels. Suggest how the speaker could improve the visual aid and delivery
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: The speaker should label the chart clearly simplify it and explain each part while facing the audience. Pausing to check understanding and inviting questions would also help.
questions.explanation: Improve clarity of the visual aid and use audience feedback during delivery.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of downward communication
questions.subject: Business Communication
options: A manager giving instructions to staff
An employee suggesting an idea to the boss
A worker complaining to a supervisor
questions.explanation: Downward communication flows from superiors to subordinates.

questions.text: Upward communication flows from subordinates to superiors
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Upward communication carries feedback and reports from lower to higher levels.

questions.text: A concise message expresses the idea using the fewest possible words without losing meaning
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Conciseness removes unnecessary words while retaining the full message.

questions.text: The study of personal space in communication is called
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Proxemics studies how distance and personal space affect communication.

questions.text: The study of the role of time in communication is called chronemics
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.explanation: Chronemics examines how the use of time conveys meaning in communication.

questions.text: Explain the difference between hearing and listening
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing is the passive physical reception of sound while listening is actively paying attention and interpreting meaning.
questions.explanation: Listening requires conscious effort and understanding unlike mere hearing.

questions.text: List any four barriers to effective listening
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Noise distractions prejudgement lack of interest and information overload.
questions.explanation: These barriers prevent the receiver from attending to and understanding the message.

questions.text: Describe the types of communication on the basis of direction
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: Communication may flow downward upward or horizontally. Downward carries orders and policies upward carries feedback and reports and horizontal links peers across departments.
questions.explanation: Explain each direction with examples and its purpose.

questions.text: Describe the process of communication with a diagram in words
questions.subject: Business Communication
questions.correctAnswer: The sender encodes an idea into a message and transmits it through a channel. The receiver decodes it and sends feedback which may be affected by noise at any stage.
questions.explanation: Trace the flow from sender through encoding channel decoding receiver and feedback.
